claims.text: HEAs have multi-principal-element compositions with a very large composition-selection space.
A deep learning-based model can be used to design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight refractory HEA compositions.
The model can predict HEA properties from composition.
The proposed model is trained using HEA compositions paired with their corresponding properties.
The training dataset is diverse and includes compositions containing refractory elements.
The training targets include strength, ductility, and weight.
Deep learning can learn complex relationships between HEA composition and properties.
Neural networks can use learned composition-property relationships to predict HEA properties.
Predicted properties can be used to identify compositions satisfying multiple desired criteria.
The model can identify RHEA compositions having at least 10% greater strength than existing RHEAs.
The model can identify RHEA compositions having at least 5% lower weight than existing RHEAs.
The predicted strength and weight improvements can be achieved while maintaining ductility.
The model's predictions are valid for HEAs containing no more than five principal elements.
The model's predictions are valid over the temperature range 500–1000 °C.
Model accuracy may be limited by the quality and diversity of the training dataset.
Model accuracy may be limited by the complexity of composition-property relationships.
The hypothesis is falsified if predictions are not within 10% of experimental measurements for at least 80% of tested compositions.
